question.text: Let $\bar{X}$ and M.D. be the mean and the mean deviation about $\bar{X}$ of $n$ observations $\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}, \mathrm{i}=1,2$,n. If each of the observations is increased by 5 , then the new mean and the mean deviation about the new mean, respectively, are :

solution.text:
Let $x_i$ be $n$ observations, $i=1,2, \ldots n$ Let $\bar{X}$ be the mean and M.D be the mean deviation about $\bar{X}$. If each observation is increased by 5 then new mean will be $\bar{X}+5$ and new M.D. about new mean will be M.D.
$$
\left(\because \text { Mean }=\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{x_i}{n}\right)
$$
